mechaber.he: דין יבם סריס וחרש שוטה וקטן וטומטום וכן היבמה. ובו טז סעיפים: סריס חמה (פירוש שנסתרס ע"י קדחת ערוך) ואיילונית (פירוש איילונית שיש לה טבע זכר כלומר שאינה יולדת ואיילונית נגזר מאיל שהוא זכר הצאן) אינם בני חליצה ויבום לפיכך איילונית ודאית שחלצה לא נפסלה לכהונה וכן סריס חמה שחלץ או שחלצו לאשתו אינו כלום: הגה היה ספק סריס חולץ ולא מחזקינן ליה בודאי סריס אלא אם ראו בו שנולד א' מסימני סריס כגון שהטיל מים ולא עשה כיפה אבל בלאו הכי יש לחוש שנתקלקל אחר לידתו וצריך לחלוץ (ריב"ש סימן תע"ד) היה לאיילונית ודאית צרה מותרת להתייבם:
mechaber.en: Someone "saris chamah" (explanation: he became impotent through a disease of fever, Aruch), and an "ayalonit" (explanation: she has a male nature, which means she cannot become pregnant, and "ayalonit" comes from "ayil" which is the male sheep [i.e. ram]), they do not have to do chalitzah and yibbum. Therefore, someone who is a definite ayalonit who does chalitzah [even though she didn't have to] is not invalid to a kohen. And similarly if someone who is impotent because if fever who does chalitzah, or [his relative when he dies] does chalitzah to his wife, it is nothing. {Rama: If it is [only] a possible saris, he does do chalitzah. And we do not assume for a definite saris, unless they see when he was born that he had one of the signs of impotence, for example they sprinkle water but does not make a covering. Buit without this, we suspect the damage happened after birth, and he must do chalitzah (Rivash Siman 474). A definite ayalonit's rival wife is permitted to her yibbum [despite the fact that the ayalonit is not].}

Tosafot answered that it is not called a beard unless his beard is full, and all the poskim agreed to this, unlike Raavad, who holds that when he has two hairs in the beard he is no longer called a saris. Tosafot's intent in what they wrote, "he has a beard," is that his beard is full; that is, if his beard is full, it is no longer possible to say that he has all the signs of a saris, and if so he is not a saris. But one can still say that nevertheless he does not have the law of an adult, but remains a minor until most of his years. Therefore I do not understand what Beit Yosef wrote at the beginning of siman 169, on the Tur's statement that if his beard is full one need not examine further; he wrote that he learned this from the above Tosafot.
